objective.text: The objective of this research was to develop and validate new flamelet generated manifold modeling techniques for concurrent flame spread in microgravity.
objective.quote: The objective of this research was to develop and validate new flamelet generated manifold (FGM) modeling techniques for concurrent flame spread in microgravity.

fuel.text: The tested materials included polymethyl methacrylate samples and wax cylinders.
fuel.quote: flat sheets, spheres, and rod-shaped polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) samples, as well as wax cylinders.

sample_geometry.text: The BASS geometries included flat sheets, spheres, and rod-shaped samples, as well as cylinders.
sample_geometry.quote: flat sheets, spheres, and rod-shaped polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) samples, as well as wax cylinders.

measurements.text: The evaluation metrics included flame geometry, temperature distribution, soot volume fraction, and flame spread rate.
measurements.quote: The evaluation metrics included flame geometry, temperature distribution, soot volume fraction, and flame spread rate, with special emphasis on reproducing the “Goldilocks” flammability zone reported by Olson and Ferkul.

safety_finding.text: The long-term goal was to enable accurate prediction of flammability limits for spacecraft materials and to provide a tool that could also serve as a subgrid-scale model in large-eddy simulations of fires, supporting spacecraft safety and hazard mitigation.
safety_finding.quote: Ultimately, the long-term goal was to enable accurate prediction of flammability limits for spacecraft materials and to provide a tool that could also serve as a subgrid-scale model in large-eddy simulations of fires, supporting spacecraft safety and hazard mitigation.

earth_benefits.text: On Earth, these advancements could improve combustion modeling by deepening our understanding of coupled thermal, chemical, and flow processes, which betters fire safety standards.
earth_benefits.quote: On Earth, these advancements could improve combustion modeling by deepening our understanding of coupled thermal, chemical, and flow processes, which betters fire safety standards.
